title: Number 81
narrativeQuestion: Who saw Aaron Hernandez coming, and does what doctors found in his brain change the story?

chapters.title: The player
chapters.claim: From Bristol to Florida to pick 113 to a $40 million extension to a 2015 murder conviction.

chapters.title: You are in the draft room
chapters.claim: Teams in 2010 had documented red flags and the Patriots took him in round four after his letter offering drug tests.

chapters.title: Odin Lloyd
chapters.claim: Odin Lloyd, 27, a semi-pro linebacker and landscaper, was killed June 17, 2013. Hernandez was convicted April 15, 2015.

chapters.title: Erasing number 81
chapters.claim: About 2,500 jerseys were exchanged on July 6 and 7, 2013, about 30 percent youth sizes, at a cost of about $250,000.

chapters.title: Guilty, erased, guilty again
chapters.claim: The conviction was vacated under abatement ab initio in May 2017 and reinstated by the Supreme Judicial Court on March 13, 2019.

chapters.title: The brain
chapters.claim: Boston University found Stage 3 CTE at age 27; the next youngest Stage 3 case they had seen was 46. McKee would not connect the disease to his crimes.

accuracyNotes: The death is stated as suicide without method, with a 988 support line.
The 2007 Gainesville incident is described as a police complaint with no formal charge.
